questions.q: What is the correct order for deploying a storage account for the first time?
options: Create a resource group first, then create the storage account inside it
Create the storage account first, then assign it to a resource group afterward
Deploy directly to a subscription with no resource group involved
Create a management group first, then a storage account
questions.explain: Every real Azure deployment starts by creating a resource group to hold the resources that go inside it.

questions.q: What does `--sku Standard_LRS` specify when creating a storage account via the CLI?
options: The redundancy/replication tier — Standard performance, Locally Redundant Storage
The region the resource is deployed to
The RBAC role assigned to the resource
The resource group's name
questions.explain: LRS is the cheapest replication option covered back in the storage overview lesson.

questions.q: What's actually different between deploying through the Portal versus through the CLI?
options: Only how you issue the request (clicking vs. typing) — both go through the same Azure Resource Manager underneath
The CLI deploys to a completely different underlying system than the Portal
The Portal cannot create storage accounts, only the CLI can
CLI-created resources are not billable, but Portal-created ones are
questions.explain: The Portal and CLI are two front doors to the exact same Resource Manager process.

questions.q: What happens to RBAC permissions when a resource deployment request reaches Azure Resource Manager?
options: Resource Manager checks your RBAC permissions at that scope before provisioning the resource
RBAC is only checked after the resource has already been created
RBAC permissions are irrelevant to resource deployment
RBAC is bypassed entirely when using the CLI instead of the Portal
questions.explain: Permission checks happen as part of the same underlying provisioning sequence, regardless of which front door was used.

questions.q: Why should a practice storage account be deleted right after confirming the deployment worked?
options: Because storage accounts are billed the moment they exist, even nearly empty, under the pay-as-you-go model
Because Azure automatically deletes all storage accounts after 24 hours
Because leaving it running would violate RBAC rules
Because storage accounts cannot be deleted once created
questions.explain: Deleting the resource group removes everything inside it in one action, avoiding ongoing charges for a resource that's no longer needed.
